narrationScript: As we discussed, linear search has a significant limitation: its worst-case and average-case time complexity are O(n). This means if you have a million items, you might perform a million checks. For large datasets and frequent searches, this is simply too slow and unacceptable. This is where Binary Search comes in, offering a dramatically more efficient approach. However, Binary Search comes with a crucial prerequisite: the data MUST be sorted. If your data isn't sorted, you'd need to sort it first, which itself takes time. Once sorted, Binary Search works on the powerful principle of 'divide and conquer.' Instead of checking elements one by one, it repeatedly halves the search interval, quickly narrowing down the possibilities.
